description: Follow-up from PX-0029 security review on storage#18. Namespace::publish currently ignores a failed first-commit previous removal and ignores journal removal after the snapshot step. If previous removal fails, revision 0 can remain rollback-able to stale state; if journal removal fails after a failed snapshot write, recovery can replay an unacknowledged commit. Decide fail-closed semantics (commit error or explicit corrupt marker), preserve journal-before-snapshot and fsync ordering, and add runnable tests that force the cleanup failure paths. Not necessary for the symlink containment fix.
title: Treat previous/journal cleanup failures as explicit commit errors

description: Follow-up from PX-0029 security review on storage#18. valid_name allows trailing-dot names (a.) and reserved device names (con, nul); on Windows a. can alias a, so two namespace names could target one directory sequentially. Linux x86_64 is the only packaged target and the anchored backend fails closed on Windows, so this is not reachable today. Add platform-specific namespace grammar rules and tests before any Windows backend is enabled.
title: Reject trailing-dot and reserved device names before Windows enablement
